column6: The Vedic religion develops in the northwest of the subcontinent in the early Vedic period.
Brahmanism develops here as an ideology that stresses ritual and the Brahmins' position.
The Magadha-based empires took in the Kuru-Panchala realm, and Brahmanism spread over a wider area.

column3: The Vedic religion develops in the northwest of the subcontinent as a variant of Indo-Aryan religion, influenced by the remnants of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Indo-Aryan people move into the Gangetic Plain and become settled farmers; the late Vedic period begins.
Brahmanism takes shape in the Ganges basin, giving priests a central place in ritual and law.
The Upanishads of the late Vedic period begin to set out the ideas of karma and rebirth.
The Vedic period is held to end; Brahmanism spreads beyond the Kuru-Panchala realm, beside the rival Shramana traditions.
